correctness.rationale: For q>=3 distinct cyclic runs and k>=1, greedy complete arches exactly equal scattered-subsequence universality. From a phase in run j, the first completing run is j+q-1 and subsequent arch endpoints advance q-1 for a nonsingleton endpoint or q for a singleton endpoint. Counting endpoint indices within the half-open k-period factor gives k+floor((k-1+delta)/(q-1)) when all runs are nonsingleton. In the singleton case the bounded deficiency E_r=rq-(J_r-j) lies in [1,q], with equality at q only for a run-start boundary, excluding a (k+1)th arch: the index is k in every phase. All maximizing-phase counts follow; q>=3, positive lengths and position rotations are essential. Independently scanned 16,200 (word, phase, repetition) cases for q=3,4,5 with run lengths 1..3 and k=1..5, matching the formulas; this finite check corroborates the full recurrence proof.
residual_risks: The proof uses the standard greedy arch universality lemma; finite checking does not establish infinite quantifiers.
